heroHeadline: Six-Month Lull Shatters: US Strikes Kermanshah and Lavan Island, Disputed Wedding Strike in Kuhestak; Iran Retaliates Across Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Iraq
heroSubtitle: Day 188 (September 2, 2026): The month-long standoff over the Strait of Hormuz erupted into the war's broadest single-day exchange since late July. On Sept 1 (Day 187), unclaimed strikes disabled two Saudi-crude VLCCs, Sidr and Senegal Prosperity, near Khasab, Oman — CENTCOM cited these tanker attacks and strikes on US forces/bases as the trigger for a new wave of US strikes on IRGC radar, maritime, and mine-laying facilities at Kermanshah (4 killed) and Lavan Island (3 killed). Iran also claims a US strike hit a wedding gathering in Kuhestak, killing 4-5 people including a child and wounding dozens; CENTCOM says it is 'looking into' the claim and denies targeting civilians. On Sept 2 (Day 188), Iran's IRGC retaliated with a coordinated missile-and-drone operation: 13 ballistic missiles at Camp Titin and Prince Hassan Air Base in Jordan (10 intercepted, no casualties), a contested drone strike on Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, suicide drones targeting Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, and a combined missile/drone attack on US-linked facilities near Erbil, Iraq. Separately, the IAEA reported it has had no nuclear verification access to Iran since the war began Feb 28, calling the unaccounted-for enriched uranium stockpile 'a matter of proliferation concern.' Brent crude surged roughly 7% over the two days to $96.59/bbl, the sharpest short-term jump since the war's early months.
